---
title: "R5. Writing a quality assurance statement"
description: "What a quality assurance statement says, with a worked example."
---

A quality assurance statement tells a reader what was done to make the analysis trustworthy, and
what its limits are. You need one at every level. Your level decides how much it carries and who
sees it.

| Level | Statement |
|---|---|
| Level 1 Standard | **Required**, and short. State your main limitation alongside the result |
| Level 2 Enhanced | Required |
| Level 3 Comprehensive | Required, and **published with the output** |
| Level 4 BCA | Required, published with the output, and covered by the quality assurance appraisal sign-off |

: What each assurance level requires of the quality assurance statement

## A worked example

This is a Level 2 Enhanced statement. Bracketed prompts show what belongs in each place.

**It is illustrative rather than approved wording.** It shows what a statement contains and what
each part is for. It has not been cleared as a form of words, so write your own from it rather
than lifting it whole.

> This analysis was produced by [analyst], [team], NHS Business Services Authority, in [month year]
> to support [the decision it informs].
>
> It was assessed as Level 2 Enhanced on the NHSBSA Analytical Assurance Decision Tool.
> The basis was that it informs a directorate-level operational decision using linked internal data
> and an established statistical method.
>
> Inputs were drawn from [source] as at [extract date]. [Named data quality issue] is present in the
> source and affects [which part of the result] by [scale or direction]. The method was independently
> reviewed by [reviewer] on [date], and the code is peer reviewed and version controlled at
> [repository].
>
> Key assumptions and their sensitivity are recorded in the project record at [link]. The principal
> limitation is [limitation], which means these results should not be used to [the specific misuse
> this analysis cannot support].
>
> Residual uncertainty is [description]. Questions about interpretation should go to [contact].

## What each level's statement carries

What a Level 3 statement carries is on [Phase 4, delivery, communication and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd). What a Level 4 BCA statement adds is on [Business Critical analysis, step 7](../08-business-critical/index.qmd#step-7-publish-what-was-checked). Both are the playbook's own requirements, so they sit with the steps that act on them.

## What GovS 010 says about the statement {#what-govs-010-says-about-the-statement}

GovS 010 section 5.5 says the results should include an assurance statement. The statement covers assumptions, uncertainty, limitations, and comments on the applicability and use of the results.[^src-govs-010-section-5-5]

GovS 010 puts the statement as a should, not a shall. The playbook requires a statement at every level, and that requirement is the playbook's own.

[^src-govs-010-section-5-5]: [GovS 010 section 5.5](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-analysis-functional-standard--2/government-functional-standard-govs-010-analysis#delivering-the-analysis)
